segments.text: Salt gets sprinkled onto an icy sidewalk.
But the weather outside hasn't gotten any warmer.
Ice always has a super-thin layer of water on its surface.
The salt dissolves right into that water, forming brine.
Saltwater freezes at a much lower temperature than plain water.
So at today's temperature, it simply can't freeze.
That brine keeps spreading and melting the ice next to it.
Because its freezing point drops, salty water just keeps melting.
